newsitem.title: DUBAI: King Fahd says Saudi to press on with development.
newsitem.headline: King Fahd says Saudi to press on with development.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's King Fahd said the oil-rich kingdom was committed to proceeding with development plans, protecting its citizens against economic hardships and meeting payments to contractors.
King Fahd said in an interview with the official Saudi Press Agency, published late on Sunday to mark the kingdom's national day on Monday, that the Saudi economy was "strong and has a solid basis.
"There is no country on the face of the earth that does not have problems or economic difficulties," the king said.
He said the government was keen to preserve "three basic issues which are the basis for our economic policies."

He listed the three as ensuring that "the citizen should not in any way be affected by the implications of economic difficulties. We will protect their interests...Second that the country meets its commitments to those dealing with it from institutions, contractors and those carrying out projects.
"The third is continuing the development process without stopping and allocating the necessary funds under the development plans," he said.
The world's largest oil producer and exporter had in recent years suffered from swings in the world prices of oil, its main source of income.

That, coupled with huge expenses in the 1990-91 Gulf crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, left the country strapped for cash and put King Fahd under pressure to introduce economic reform and start planning for privatisation and less spending.

In 1995 King Fahd told Saudis -- once used to lavish state benefits -- that unprecedented price rises introduced that year for basic services such as water and electricity were temporary. Riyadh also began issuing special bonds to make a dent in the estimated $3.5 billion outstanding to contractors.
